Definition: of Hebrew origin (H1834); Damascus, a city of Syria:--Damascus.
BiblicalUsage: Damascus is the city of Paul's conversion, named fifteen times in the New Testament. He was on the road there, breathing threats, when the light struck him down; Ananias was sent to him there; and he preached Christ in its synagogues at once, so that the Jews took counsel to kill him. It is the city where the persecutor became the preacher.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Damascus is where grace interrupts a life mid-stride. The road to Damascus is my picture of conversion: Christ meets a man going the wrong way and turns him around in a moment.
